neighbours.label: a body part or component named as the feature being characterised in a morphological description (the number of wheels; legs short and sturdy; tail and rump concolorous), not the same noun in a narrated event
fire: Spiders differ from insects chiefly in the number of legs they carry on the thorax.
This pony is stocky, with a thick neck, and the legs are short and strong.
The lizard is slender and olive green, with tail and hind limbs noticeably long.
Compared with the sedan, the main change in the truck is the number of axles under the bed.
The adult moth is pale grey, with antennae feathery and the wings narrow.
Sloths are classified into two groups according to the number of toes on the front feet.
The stork is a tall white bird, and the bill is long, straight and red.
The newer scooter is wider, and its extra wheels are small and set close together.
quiet: The spider hurt one of its legs when the jar tipped over on the shelf.
The pony kicked its legs and bolted across the yard when the gate opened.
The lizard dropped its tail and vanished under the rocks before we could move.
The mechanic took the wheels off the truck and stacked them beside the bed.
The moth beat its wings against the lamp until someone opened the window.
The sloth scratched its toes on the bark and climbed slowly out of reach.
The stork snapped its bill at the dog and flew off over the marsh.
The boy sold the scooter and its spare wheels to a neighbour for twenty dollars.

notes: Card: tail/rump, wheels, anthers, toothless, hind-limbs, Legs in descriptive anatomy/design text.
